PRAYING TO ALLOW THE PETITION AND ORDER TO RELEASE THE  PETITIONER/ACCUSED ON BAIL IN S.C. NO.5086/2023 FOR THE  ALLEGED OFFENCES U/S 498A, 304B OF IPC AND SECTION 3 AND 4  OF DP ACT, PENDING ON THE FILE OF I ADDITIONAL DISTRICT AND  SESSIONS JUDGE, DHARWAD, SITTING AT HUBBALLI.
 THIS CRIMINAL PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS  DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 -2-  NC: 2024:KHC-D:3845  CRL.P No. 103302 of 2023  ORDER Heard Shri. S. S. Yadrami, learned Senior Counsel and Shri. Praveen Y. Devaraddiyavar, learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent - State.
2. Successive bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short 'Cr.P.C.').
Earlier bail application was dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to file bail application after filling of the charge sheet.
Since the charge sheet is now filed, the accused has renewed his request for bail with a successive bail application.

3. Shri. S. S. Yadrami, learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner, reiterating the bail grounds contended that the material on record would not warrant continuation of the accused in judicial custody any longer and sought for allowing the bail application.,
4.

He also took the Court through the charge sheet materials and demonstrated that there is a deviation from the complaint averments and the charge sheet materials and therefore the petitioner/accused need not be retained in the judicial custody as the Investigating Officer has already recorded the statements of all the witnesses.

He further pointed out that a 3 years old child is born in the wedlock of deceased and the petitioner/accused and at present the said child is under care and custody of the grandmother of the child who is aged about 80 years and a poor vision and hearing.
As such, there is nobody to look after the young child and therefore, using the discretionary powers vested in this Court under Section 439 of Cr.P.C., this Court may enlarge the petitioner on bail.
6. He also submits that any condition that would be imposed by this Court would be impatiently obeyed by the petitioner and sought for granting bail.

Santosh S/O. Laxman Katti vs The State Of Karnataka on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35367148/
2 7.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader opposes the bail request by contending that the incident has occurred in the house of the accused and by that time the complainant visited the house of the accused, the deceased was already brought down from the hanging position and based on the information received from the others the complainant who is the brother of the deceased has lodged the complaint.

8. Later on investigation agency has collected further information and filed the charge sheet against the accused for NC: 2024:KHC-D:3845 the offence punishable under Sections 306 and 304B of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short 'IPC').
9.

He also pointed out since the incident has taken place within the seven years of the marriage prosecution enjoys the presumption as to dowry death and there are materials to establish the dowry death.
10. He further contended that unless the material witnesses are examined, enlarging the accused/petitioner on bail would definitely hamper the case of the prosecution to a considerable extent.
As such apprehension on behalf of the prosecution is well founded having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case on hand and sought for dismissal of the bail petition.
11. Having heard the parties in detail, this Court perused the material on record meticulously.
12. As rightly contended by Shri. S. S. Yadrami, learned Senior Counsel for petitioner, filing of a charge sheet is a changed circumstance in a criminal trial.

13. However, it is equally well settled that filing of a charge sheet in every case would not act as a positive changed circumstance so as to allow the accused/petitioner to obtain an NC:
2024:KHC-D:3845 order of grant of bail by resorting to the special powers vested in this Court under Section 439 of Cr.P.C.
14.
Since the death has taken place in the house of the husband, according to the prosecution it is a suicidal death and death has also taken place within seven years of the marriage
, learned Public Prosecutor is justified in contending that the prosecution enjoys the presumption that the death of the deceased is a dowry death.

15. Material on record especially complaint averments and further statements of the complaint and statement of the witnesses at the time of inquest and at the time of Investigating Officer investigating the matter, prima facie, points finger towards the guilt of the accused as to the demand of dowry is concerned.

16. Whether at all there were any compelling reasons for the deceased to commit suicide that too in the house of the accused/petitioner forgetting that she has got a 3 years old child is a question that is to be decided during the Trial.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 17. Prima facie materials at this stage especially in the absence of conclusive findings either in the form of Post Mortem Report or any other material on record as to the cause NC: 2024:KHC-D:3845 of death, this Court is unable to accept the version of the accused/petitioner for that matter of the opposition of the prosecution.

18. Having regard to the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case, if the material witnesses are directed to be examined within a period of two months and if any positive changed circumstances there in the case of the accused/petitioner, permitting him to renew the bail request with a successive bail application would thus be right and justifiable course in the facts and circumstances of the case on hand.
19. Expressing any opinion at this point of time either in favour of the prosecution or against the prosecution would definitely hamper the rights of the respective parties during the trial.

20. Thus, desisting from holding a mini trial, directing the Trial Court to expedite the trail in a time bound manner with liberty for the petitioner to renew his request if there is a positive changed circumstances would meet the ends of justice.

Accordingly, the following order is passed:
ORDER (i) Bail petition is rejected.
(ii) The Trial Court is directed to expedite the trial and positively examine the material witnesses on or before 30.04.2024.
(iii) In the event of any positive changed circumstances after examination of the material witnesses, the petitioner is at liberty to apply for bail with successive bail request.
(iv) Observation made by this Court during the course of this order shall not influence the learned Trial Judge in the trial.

Sd/-
